# Classes

Every class the stylesheet defines, in the sections the stylesheet itself uses. The class names match igni's own: a control here is the control there.

## The page

| Class | Selector | What it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `.igni-root` | `.igni-root` | `margin`, `background`, `color`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `line-height` |

## Primitives

The shapes this app keeps making, named once. They were not extracted from duplication, because there was very little: the 231 classes called `-row`, `-card`, `-actions` share almost nothing — `*-row` agreed only on `display: flex`, and deduplicating all fourteen patterns saved 84 declarations out of 17,789 lines. They did not repeat. They diverged, each feature picking its own gaps and paddings because there was no scale to pick from. So these are decided rather than derived. Where the existing uses agreed, the agreement is the value. Where they split, the split is resolved here with a reason, once, instead of in each feature. There is deliberately no `ui-title`. Titles varied across four type steps and that variation is the design — a heading level, not drift. Use the type scale and a weight.

| Class | Selector | What it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `.ui-row` | `.ui-row` | `display`, `align-items`, `gap` |
| `.ui-actions` | `.ui-actions` | `display`, `align-items`, `gap` |
| `.ui-list` | `.ui-list` | `display`, `flex-direction`, `gap` |
| `.ui-toolbar` | `.ui-toolbar` | `display`, `align-items`, `gap` |
| `.ui-card` | `.ui-card` | `display`, `flex-direction`, `gap`, `padding`, `background`, `border`, `border-radius` |
| `.ui-item` | `.ui-item` | `padding`, `border-radius`, `color`, `text-align`, `cursor` |
| `.ui-item` | `.ui-item:hover` | `background` |
| `.ui-badge` | `.ui-badge` | `display`, `align-items`, `gap`, `padding`, `border-radius`, `font-size`, `font-weight` |
| `.ui-empty` | `.ui-empty` | `color`, `font-size` |

## MarkdownInline

Rendered markdown flattened to one run of text, for previews. Every rule here exists to keep the content *inline*: the row that holds it clamps to two lines, and a single block-level child inside that breaks the clamp — the preview grows to the document's full height and the list stops being a list.

## MermaidBlock

Mermaid produces its own SVG with embedded styles tuned for a light background — we frame it with the standard inset surface and clip overly wide diagrams with horizontal scroll. `mermaid` is a peer dependency, imported on demand: a page with no diagram in it never downloads the 700KB.

## Tier 0: the page itself

`.igni-root` used to set colour and type and stop. No height, no box-sizing, nothing on `html`. A full-frame extension therefore began by writing the same six lines every other extension writes, and wrote them differently — which is how two panels in one app end up scrolling differently. These rules are the floor taking responsibility for the page. They are safe on a page that does not want them: a short document still flows, because the height rules only matter once something inside asks to fill.

| Class | Selector | What it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `.igni-root` | `.igni-root` | `min-height`, `box-sizing` |
| `.igni-root` | `.igni-root *` | `box-sizing` |
| `.igni-root` | `.igni-root *::before` | `box-sizing` |
| `.igni-root` | `.igni-root *::after` | `box-sizing` |
| `.ui-shell` | `.ui-shell` | `display`, `flex-direction`, `height`, `min-height` |
| `.ui-shell-header` | `.ui-shell-header` | `flex` |
| `.ui-shell-footer` | `.ui-shell-footer` | `flex` |

## Tier 0: selection

`.ui-item` had hover and focus and nothing for *selected*, which is the entire interaction model of a two-pane browser: a list on the left, and the thing you picked still showing which one it was. Without this every extension invents its own highlight, and they differ from igni and from each other. Driven by the ARIA attribute rather than a class, so the thing that makes it look selected is the same thing that makes it announce as selected. A row that looks picked and reads as not picked is the bug this shape prevents.

| Class | Selector | What it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `.ui-item` | `.ui-item[aria-selected="true"]` | `background`, `color` |

| `.ui-item` | `.ui-item[aria-current]:not([aria-current="false"])` | `box-shadow` |

## Split

Two panes and a rule you can move. The width lives in a custom property the component writes, so dragging reflows the browser and never re-renders the tree. The property is named per instance, which is why there is no literal here: two splits on one page would otherwise fight over one variable.

| Class | Selector | What it sets |
|---|---|---|
| `.ui-split` | `.ui-split` | `display`, `grid-template-columns`, `flex`, `min-height` |
| `.ui-split-end` | `.ui-split-end` | `grid-template-columns` |
| `.ui-split-aside` | `.ui-split-aside` | `min-width`, `min-height`, `display`, `flex-direction` |
| `.ui-split-main` | `.ui-split-main` | `min-width`, `min-height`, `display`, `flex-direction` |
| `.ui-split-main` | `.ui-split-main` | `border-left` |
| `.ui-split-end` | `.ui-split-end .ui-split-main` | `border-left`, `border-right` |
| `.ui-split-handle` | `.ui-split-handle` | `cursor`, `background`, `margin`, `z-index`, `touch-action` |
| `.ui-split-handle` | `.ui-split-handle:hover` | `background`, `outline` |
| `.ui-split-handle` | `.ui-split-handle:focus-visible` | `background`, `outline` |
| `.ui-split-resizing` | `.ui-split-resizing` | `cursor`, `user-select` |

## Prose

What rendered markdown looks like. The floor published `MarkdownInline`, which flattens block structure by design — right for a two-line preview and exactly wrong for a document. So an extension with prose in it bundled its own renderer and then had nothing to style it against, because igni's prose rules live in `theme.css` and are not in the floor. These are. They are deliberately plain: a document surface is the extension's, and what the floor owes is type that matches the rest of the app.
